subject: Quota & surge plan for BrightPath launch - action items & product clarifications
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: ops+platform@brightpathhealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Launch traffic & quota request for Oct 5 launch

Hi Priyom —

Quick intro: BrightPath is planning to flip a new triage feature into production for a pilot cohort on Oct 5. Ops asked me to reach out for a quota/rate uplift and a short runbook so we don’t hit hard throttles during the initial ramp.

Key numbers from our end (attached spreadsheet "BrightPath_Beta_Traffic_v1.xlsx"):
- Peak concurrent API sessions: ~1,200 (expected during 10am–2pm PST window)
- Estimated requests per second (API calls to Redwood): 180 rps during peak, avg 45 rps otherwise
- Request type mix: 60% short prompts (~150 tokens output), 40% long-form (avg 800 tokens output) — function calling used in ~30% of long-form flows
- Expected 10-day warmup profile (see tab "ramp" in the sheet)

Asks:
1) Temporary quota bump for Oct 5–Oct 12 to avoid 429s while we validate the ramp
2) Recommended canary schedule (we’d like to start at 5% traffic and double every 12 hours)
3) Any product constraints we should be aware of (function-calling token multipliers, recommended model variants for cost/latency)

We also need a short mutual action plan and a single-runbook PDF that our SREs can follow if we see latency spikes. Can you loop in the right folks for capacity and product clarifications?

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Platform Integrations
BrightPath Health

Attachment: BrightPath_Beta_Traffic_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 230KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Susan Park <susan.park@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch traffic & quota request for Oct 5 launch

Folks — looping you in. Summary: BrightPath is planning a pilot flip on Oct 5 and expects a short (7–10 day) warmup with a peak ~180 rps and mixed token profiles. They want a temporary quota bump and a concise operational runbook.

Immediate asks for infra/product:
- Capacity: can we provide a temporary quota bump to handle 200 rps peak and token headroom for function-calling bursts? If so, what are the exact numeric bump values (tokens/sec, concurrent sessions) and for what time window?
- Routing/model: recommend a cost/latency model variant (quantized vs fp16) for their mix — product: is there a recommended default?
- Runbook: I drafted a short runbook (attached "redwood_proposed_runbook_v1.md") with steps for canary sizing, rollback thresholds (5xx rate >1.5% or p95 latency >600ms for more than 5 minutes), and escalation path. Please review.

Karthik — can your team confirm whether a hosted temporary uplift or a Reserved Dedicated warmup is better here? If hosted, what lead time do we need to guarantee the uplift for Oct 5 9am PST?

Neha — if we need a short SLA exception (lowered throttle sensitivity) for the week, can you flag next steps for approvals?

I’ll reply to Susan once we have alignment on numeric limits and canary timing.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_proposed_runbook_v1.md (text, 4KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch traffic & quota request for Oct 5 launch

Thanks — ran the numbers with infra. Quick answers:
- Short-term uplift: we can provision a hosted temporary uplift for the Oct 5–Oct 12 window. Proposed numeric uplift:
  * Token throughput: +120M tokens/day (approx) allocated to BrightPath account for the 7-day window
  * Request RPS soft-cap: raise to 250 rps peak, with standard throttling after that
  * Concurrent sessions guard: allow 1,500 concurrent sessions for the week

- Lead time: we need the final confirmation by EOD Tue Sep 22 to reserve capacity and adjust autoscaling knobs. If they need earlier, we can prioritize but it will require operational overtime.

- Performance profile: for their mix (short + long + function calls), recommend using our q4_12b-optimized variant (quantized) — balance of token cost and p95 latency. Function-calling can increase output tokens by ~1.7x on average; factor that into totals.

- Fallbacks: we can configure automated fallback to a lower-cost variant (q3_7b) if token burn exceeds 110% of daily allocation, with an opt-in grace period of 30 minutes before hard throttles.

I’ve attached a short patch to the runbook with the numeric values and rollback thresholds.

— Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
Attachment: redwood_proposed_runbook_v1.md (updated, 6KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference.com>, Susan Park <susan.park@brightpathhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch traffic & quota request for Oct 5 launch

Susan / team — quick product notes so expectations are clear:
1) Function-calling impact: any flow that triggers tool calls and structured JSON completions will increase output tokens significantly. Recommend reducing max_response_tokens in function-calling flows for the canary.
2) Model knobs: q4_12b-optimized is the right default for latency/cost tradeoff. If BrightPath is extremely latency-sensitive in the 10am–2pm window, we can pin a small pool of dedicated capacity (reserved nodes) for the highest percentiles; that requires a short committed reservation.
3) Prompt design: small prompt-level changes (strip long system instructions for short prompts) can reduce average output tokens by ~12–18% — include this in the BrightPath preflight checklist.

Can we get BrightPath ops to confirm the canary cadence (5% -> 10% -> 20% -> 40% -> 80% -> 100%) and the time between steps? If they prefer doubling every 12 hours, we’ll build the runbook around that.

I’ll update the runbook with the model knob recommendations and a quick checklist for their SREs.

— Lauren
Product Manager, Serving Runtime

> On Sep 18, 2026, at 10:05, Priyom Das wrote:
> > I drafted a short runbook (attached "redwood_proposed_runbook_v1.md") with steps for canary sizing, rollback thresholds ...

Attachment: BrightPath_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (pdf, 28KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@brightpathhealth.com>, ops+platform@brightpathhealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Launch traffic & quota request for Oct 5 launch

Susan — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick summary and next steps (mutual action plan):

What we’ll provide (Oct 5–Oct 12):
- Temporary hosted uplift: token allocation +120M/day, peak RPS soft-cap raised to 250, concurrent sessions allowed up to 1,500
- Canary schedule: 5% -> 10% (12h) -> 20% (12h) -> 40% (12h) -> 80% (12h) -> 100%
- Rollback thresholds: p95 > 600ms for 5 minutes OR 5xx > 1.5% for 5 minutes -> immediate rollback to previous canary step
- Fallback: automated routing to q3_7b if token burn exceeds 110% of daily allocation (30-minute grace)

Customer asks for action:
- Confirm the canary cadence (do you want 12-hour steps?)
- Confirm that you can reduce max_response_tokens for function-calling flows during canary (recommended)
- Sign mutual action plan (Doc link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/brightpath-health) so we can schedule the uplift on Sep 22 (deadline for provisioning)

Operational notes: Karthik’s team will provision the uplift after confirmation. Lauren will update the runbook with the model recommendations. Neha — please flag any approvals required for the SLA exception and quota window.

If we don’t hear back by Tue Sep 22 EOD we can still try to prioritize but cannot guarantee reserved warm nodes for the 10am PST ramp.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth roll.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
